chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from al-'Ala' and Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

In the case of two men who testified on behalf of a man whose wife was absent, that he had divorced her, so the woman observed the waiting period and married another. Then the absent husband returned and claimed he had not divorced her, and one of the two witnesses proved him a liar. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The other [witness] has no claim upon her, and the dowry is taken from the one who testified and returned to the other, and they are separated. She observes the waiting period from the latter [husband], and the first [husband] does not approach her until her waiting period is completed.'

key_terms.اعْتَدَّتِ الْمَرْأَةُ: The woman observed the waiting period (iddah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when an absent husband's divorce is testified by two witnesses, but one witness is later proven false?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of 'presumption of validity' (istishab) in Shia jurisprudence, where the initial marriage remains valid until proven otherwise by reliable testimony. It highlights the practical legal consequence of witness credibility: the false witness bears the financial penalty by transferring his dowry to the truthful one, ensuring the wife's status is clarified through the second marriage's waiting period (iddah). This ruling underscores the importance of evidentiary standards in resolving marital disputes in the absence of the husband.
